lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Noon in the Sunscar. The sand has turned to glass in places, and the light comes up off it as hard as it comes down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the Tent of Cool Water, a veiled elder waits at the flap, holding a clay bowl in both hands.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Well, look who crossed the desert. I was beginning to think I'd have to give you a sad ending.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Quickly, before she's offended. Drink half the water. Pour the rest on the sand, for the farms that burned.

options.label: We drink half, and pour the rest out.
I'll sing the guest-song Lark taught me.
Why pour it away? Water's precious out here.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: That's the point. You give the sand something you can't spare. Then they give you everything they have.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Half the water goes to the party and half to the sand. The elder watches until the last drop sinks into the glass.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The old tune rises over the tents and heads turn. Somewhere behind the elder's veil, someone starts to hum along.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Every note. Well, you mangled the second verse, but only a little.
lines.direction: proud, and trying to hide it

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The elder lowers the bowl and speaks the law of the tent, slowly, so that strangers can follow.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: While you sleep under this cloth, every Scarwalker in the Sunscar will bleed for you.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Break the peace inside this camp, and no Scarwalker will ever speak your names again. Not your children's, either.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Over flatbread and bitter tea, the elder tells the party what the desert knows, and Lark puts it into the valley tongue.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: The only road to the crater crosses the canyon, and the only bridge belongs to a goblin called Vorga. He took it in spring.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: His Host lets the Scarwalker caravans over to the wells, then keeps the water. A toll, he calls it. The elder has another word.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the fire, a hobgoblin in a sun-painted sash sips from the same clay bowl, and pretends not to listen.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Yes, he's one of Vorga's. Yes, he's a guest. No, you can't. Let the poor thing finish his tea.
lines.direction: quick, amused, a hand on someone's arm

options.label: Tell us about Vorga.
Ask the hobgoblin to take Vorga a message.
Has anyone else come this way?
I know the hill clans. A war band isn't a clan.
We've heard enough. We sleep, and go at dawn.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Young, loud, very fond of his own voice. He sends the Scarwalkers a song every new moon about how he's going to eat them.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Terrible song. Good rhythm, though. And under all the shouting, he's angrier than anyone I've ever met.
lines.direction: the joke fading as it goes

options.label: Does he know we made peace with his grandmother?
Does he know what happened at the ford?

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: He knows. He's telling the whole canyon she sold the clan for a few sacks of grain, and that you're holding the leash.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: The lads who fought you at the ford were his. The ones who made it home haven't stopped talking about you.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: He knows. He doesn't sing about the Scarwalkers any more. All the new verses are about you.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Whatever he thought of her, she was his grandmother. Nobody else was allowed to kill her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The hobgoblin hears the party out, sets down his bowl, and answers in a low, careful voice.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: He says Vorga will be delighted to meet you. He says to bring rope. He seems to think that's funny.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: A Kindled caravan, nine days ago, under a white cloth. The elder gave them water, because the law says she must.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Their leader asked after you by name. Lovely voice. Kind eyes. I didn't like how much I liked her.
lines.direction: uneasy, trying to make it a joke

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: No. A clan has grandmothers. Vorga's Host is everyone who got tired of waiting for the grandmothers.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Anything else, before the tea runs out?

options.label: Tell us about Vorga.
Ask the hobgoblin to take Vorga a message.
Has anyone else come this way?
I know the hill clans. A war band isn't a clan.
We've heard enough. We sleep, and go at dawn.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Night comes down cold and fast. Under the Tent of Cool Water, for the first time in weeks, the party sleeps without a watch.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Nothing in the Sunscar would dare touch you tonight. Tomorrow is another song.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before dawn, a goblin boy staggers into camp, lips cracked, asking in the hill tongue for the people who brought the grain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He drinks, then shuts his eyes and gives his message the way Mother Skarrow made him learn it: slowly, in her own words.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: You fed my children, valley people. So I give you what I do not give to strangers. The rest of the song.
lines.direction: her words through the runner; her slow, deliberate cadence

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Seven went over the Greywall in the long winters, and seven came back with fire. They came back running.
lines.direction: half chanted, as a song is remembered

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: The song says the fire had a home on the far side of the mountains. The seven took it. It was not theirs to take.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Your Wardens sang that it was given. We never warmed our hands at it, so we never forgot. It was stolen.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: That's it. That's the verse before the last. I've been looking for it for twenty years.

options.label: Is there more? Does it say who they took it from?
I dream of a fire. I think this song is about where I came from.
I was on the ford bridge that day. Tell her it was our side that shot first.
Go on. What else did she say?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The boy shakes his head. The last verse belongs to the clan, he says, and the clan has only just started trusting you.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Of course it does. Of course she has.
lines.direction: laughing at themself, a little hurt

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Then someone else will want very badly to hear that dream. Be careful who you tell it to.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The boy studies the soldier for a long moment. Then he nods, once, as if he will carry that home too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The boy opens his eyes. The last part, he says, is not the song.

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: My grandson Vorga holds the bridge you need. He is a fool and a thief, and he is mine.
lines.direction: through the runner; the courtesy slips, and this is a grandmother

lines.speaker: mother_skarrow
lines.text: Do not kill him, if you can help it. Beat him if you must. Then send him home to me.

options.label: Tell her we'll try.
Tell her he'll come home. We promise.
We can't promise. That's for Vorga to decide, not us.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Big promise. Goblins remember promises. So do songs.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Honest. I think she'll like that better than a promise.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The boy repeats it twice to be sure he has it. Then he curls up by the fire, asleep before his tea is cold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The canyon road ends at a bridge of rope and old timber. On the far side stands a wall of shields painted with suns.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A goblin in a chieftain's coat three sizes too big strolls out to the end of the bridge and throws his arms wide.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: The grain-carriers! Grandmother's new friends! Did she send you all this way to ask me nicely?
lines.direction: big and theatrical, playing to his warband

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: My lads at the ford said you fought well. The ones who came back said it, anyway.
lines.direction: the grin stays; the voice drops

options.label: She wants you home, Vorga.
We need to cross. We're not here for you.
Stand aside, and let Emberwick prove it can share.
I was on the ford bridge. It was our side that shot first.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Home to what? A hill full of thank-yous and a third of a sack each? She bargains, and the little ones get thinner.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: I buried three cousins while she was being reasonable. Tell her I love her. Tell her she's wrong.
lines.direction: fast, before he can stop himself

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Everyone's here for me. It's the only bridge! The toll is everything you're carrying, and your boots.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: No, keep the boots. I'm feeling generous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For a breath Vorga doesn't answer. Behind him, the Host's warriors glance at one another.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: If I let you over, they stop believing me. And then what am I? A hungry boy on a bridge.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Lovely speech. Emberwick makes lovely speeches. Then it locks the granary and makes them again next year.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Huh. That's the first time anyone from the valley has said it out loud.
lines.direction: caught off guard, the swagger gone for a moment

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Changes nothing. But I'll remember you said it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vorga raises his spear, and up on the ridge the Host's drums begin.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The canyon road ends at a bridge of rope and old timber. On the far side stands a wall of shields painted with suns.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A goblin in a chieftain's coat three sizes too big walks out to the end of the bridge, and stops, and stares.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Oh, it's you. I practised a whole speech for this. Give me a moment, it's a good one.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: She was chief for forty winters. You ended it in an afternoon, on a bridge, over grain.
lines.direction: the speech falls apart into real anger

options.label: We're sorry about your grandmother.
We need the bridge. That's all.
Stand aside, or go the way she did.
I was on the ford bridge. It was our side that shot first.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Sorry! Hear that, everyone? They're sorry!
lines.direction: playing to the Host, laughing too loud

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Keep it. Sorry doesn't feed anyone. She tried words for forty winters, and look where it got her.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: That's all, they say! The road, the grain, the hills, my grandmother. That's all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A few spears on the far bank waver. Vorga sees it, and laughs louder to cover it.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: See that, lads? Take a good look. That's what Emberwick looks like up close.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: There's the valley talking. Threats, then grain, then threats again. At least mine are honest.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Your side shot first. Then your side came back and finished it. Do you want a medal for remembering?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He lifts his grandmother's carved spear, and up on the ridge the Host's drums begin.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bridge is gone. Below the stepping stones, Vorga kneels in the shallows, spear snapped, the river pulling at his coat.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Ha. Well. That went about as well as the bridge did.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Go on. The Host is watching from the ridge. At least make it look good.

options.label: Why cut the ropes? You nearly drowned your own warriors.
Your grandmother asked us to spare you.
Let you go, and you'll raid the river towns before winter.
Enough. We'll decide.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Because it was mine. If I can't hold it, nobody walks over it smiling. Not you, not the Kindled, nobody.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: She sent you. Of course she did. She always sends someone else to carry things.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Is she eating? Tell me she's eating, at least.
lines.direction: very quietly; no audience for this one

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Only the towns that lock their granaries. Which, I'll grant you, is all of them.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Take your time. I'm not going anywhere. Mostly because of the leg.

options.label: Why cut the ropes? You nearly drowned your own warriors.
Your grandmother asked us to spare you.
Let you go, and you'll raid the river towns before winter.
Enough. We'll decide.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Up on the ridge the Host watches in silence. Vorga waits in the river, still grinning, water to his waist.

options.label: Send him home to his grandmother.
End it here.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Home. Tail in the river and a valley mercy on my back. She'll never let me forget it.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: I'll remember who did this. I haven't decided yet whether that's a threat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By nightfall the Host's fires on the ridge go out one by one, as the war band breaks up and drifts home to the hills.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Tell her I held it longer than anyone thought I would.
lines.direction: still smiling; the last laugh doesn't come

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Host scatters into the canyons. In the hills above the ford, a runner will carry this home too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the truce Emberwick bought with grain will have to bear the weight of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bridge is gone. Below the stepping stones, Vorga kneels in the shallows, spear snapped, the river pulling at his coat.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Ha! Beaten by the same people twice. Grandmother and grandson both. Somebody should write that down.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Go on, finish the set. The Host is watching. Make it a good story for them.

options.label: Why cut the ropes? You nearly drowned your own warriors.
She wouldn't have wanted this for you.
Let you go, and you'll raid the river towns before winter.
Enough. We'll decide.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Because it was mine. If I can't hold it, nobody walks over it smiling. Not you, not the Kindled, nobody.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: You don't get to tell me what she wanted. You don't get to have that too.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Only the towns that lock their granaries. Which, I'll grant you, is all of them.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Take your time. I'm not going anywhere. Mostly because of the leg.

options.label: Why cut the ropes? You nearly drowned your own warriors.
She wouldn't have wanted this for you.
Let you go, and you'll raid the river towns before winter.
Enough. We'll decide.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Up on the ridge the Host watches in silence. Vorga waits in the river, still grinning, water to his waist.

options.label: Send him home to his clan.
End it here.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Home. There's nobody there now to tell me I was wrong. That's the worst part, you know.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: I'll remember who let me walk. I haven't decided yet what that means.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vorga limps east into the canyons. Some of the Host follow him. He doesn't look back to count them.

lines.speaker: vorga
lines.text: Put me next to her, if you can remember where you left her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Host scatters into the canyons, and the road to the crater lies open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Half a day past the canyon, the sand gives way to a stair cut into old stone. At the bottom, a door marked with the Wardens' flame.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Its seal is older than the Fall. But someone has dug the stair clear, recently, and gone in.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Every Warden song I know ends at a door like this. None of them say what's behind it. That ought to worry me more.

options.label: Dwarven work. Let me read the stone.
There's a mechanism in that seal. I can open it quietly.
We'll look for another way in.
We go through the door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The carving is a mason's warning in the old clan script: the dead keep this watch, and keep it still. Below it, a hidden latch.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Lovely. I'll put that in the chorus.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door slides aside without a sound. Rows of bone Wardens stand at their posts, and on the dais, someone is chanting.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Somebody woke them before we got here. And somebody is still here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door grinds open like a mountain clearing its throat. Below, in the dark, every bone Warden turns its head.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Ah. Well. They know we're here, then.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last bone Warden falls, and the crypt is still. Beyond the dais lies a vault of shelves, dry as the day it was sealed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No ember-lamp ever burned down here. The Wardens wrote by daylight from a shaft in the roof, and the pages are still white.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Nothing has touched these. No fire at all. Do you know how rare that is in this Vale?
lines.direction: hushed, as if in a chapel

options.label: We'll find the oldest records.
I know how the Church shelves its oldest texts. Let me look.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the oldest shelf lies a Keeper's ledger in a careful, tired hand. It is dated a hundred and eighty years after the Lighting.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Old pages crumble under hurried hands, and an hour goes to dust. Then Lark lifts down a ledger in a careful, tired hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It reads: We have learned what the fire takes. Each time it is used, it burns a memory away, and it does not give it back.
lines.direction: reading aloud, slow; a dead Keeper's words

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A smith forgets his trade. A mother forgets her son's face. A whole village forgets the road it came by.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Vale cannot live without the flame. Therefore the Vale must not know its price. So ordered, and so sealed.
lines.direction: the last words of the page, flat

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Every hearth. Every forge. Every ember-lamp in every window, for three hundred years.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: That's why the songs are all that's left. Nobody ever needed a fire to remember a tune.
lines.direction: working it out as they say it; the voice gives a little

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Bree's hearth. Corvin's missing years. Pip, born on the warm bank, remembering things that never happened to her.

options.label: We paid the Court a memory in Mirewood. At least we knew what we were giving.
We paid the Court with a memory that wasn't ours. Whose was it?
We walked away from the Court's price. Nobody here was ever offered the choice.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: You knew. You chose. Ysolde told you the price to your face, which makes her the most honest thing in this whole Vale.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Somebody's. Somebody who was never asked either. It turns out we've all been paying with other people's memories.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: No. They lit the lamps and warmed their hands, and nobody ever told them there was a bill.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Against the inner seal sit the bones of a Warden who never got it open. Under one hand is a last page, written in a hurry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is dated the night of the Fall. The Keep is burning. Warden Marrowby ran with the vault chest. I saw her go, and could not stop her.
lines.direction: reading; the hand on the page was shaking

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Marrowby. Celandine Marrowby. She's older than anyone in Emberwick, and remembers less than any of them.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: A hundred years of ember-lamps in every hall she owns. She's burned that night away. She doesn't know what she did.

options.label: My family's fortune came from the Marrowbys. From this.
The Church calls the fire a gift. The Wardens knew it was a debt, and hid it.
Whatever the gods gave the Vale, it wasn't this.
Corvin's page. My own lost pages. We found this before, and the fire took it back.
I never once used the fire. Maybe that's why I still remember everything.
Take the ledger and the page. The Vale should read them.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Then you've a choice to make. Truth is heavy. Gold's heavier, if you're the one carrying it.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Mother Aubrine will need you to say that gently. And then she'll need you to say it again.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: The gods might well agree. The Wardens don't seem to have asked them.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: You and Corvin found it twice and lost it twice. This time it's on a page no fire has ever touched.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: Then hold on to it. You may be the only one of us who'll notice when something goes missing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the party climbs back into the light, the Hooded Stranger is sitting on the top step, as if they have waited there all day.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: You've been reading. It shows. People wear that look when they've dug up a debt.

options.label: You knew. All this time, you knew.
Why are you here now?

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Would you have believed it from a stranger in a hood, in a warm inn, with all the lamps lit?

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: People only believe what they dig up themselves. So you had to dig.

lines.speaker: hooded_stranger
lines.text: Someone ought to be waiting at the top of the stair. It's a long climb, carrying a thing like that.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: I'm going to write a song about this. Nobody is going to want to hear it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crater is a bowl of black glass, too bright to look at. At its edge a white cloth hangs from a spear, and a woman waits beside it.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: You came. I hoped you would. Sit on this side, the glass is cooler, and the Scarwalkers can see we're keeping the truce.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: You've been in the crypt. I can see it on you. Everyone has that look, the day they learn what the fire takes.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I learned it thirty years ago, when a shard nearly killed me. I woke up remembering winters I never lived.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Ask me anything. I'd rather you heard it from me than from a pulpit.

options.label: You know the price, and you still want to relight it?
You feed people to it.
We paid Ysolde a memory. We know what it costs.
We paid Ysolde with a memory that wasn't ours.
We left Mirewood's ember with the Court.
The fire was stolen. The Skarrow song says so.
We sent Vorga home.
Vorga's dead. We did it.
Rook can't have that many shards to sell you. Where do they come from?
Emberwick is starving. What does your plan do for them this winter?
What do you want from us, Maren?

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Every fire costs something. The cold costs more. I've buried children who forgot nothing, because they never lived long enough to.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: A memory for a harvest. I'd make that trade for every child in the Vale. I have made it, over and over.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I feed it the willing, and I won't pretend that's clean. I hold their hands. I keep their names, for as long as I can.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Ten thousand people will freeze if I don't. I can count. Some nights I wish I couldn't.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Then you know it's bearable. You're still here. You're still yourselves, mostly. That's all I'm asking of the Vale.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: So did I, once. It frightened me how easy it was. It should frighten you a little, too.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I know. So I'll have to go back for it, and Ysolde will make me pay. I wish it had been you.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Stolen or given, it kept the Vale alive for three hundred years. I can't hand back three centuries of warm children.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: If someone over the mountains wants it, let them come and ask. I'll tell them how cold it's been without it.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Good. I offered him bread for that bridge, and he threw it in the canyon. I liked him for it.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I'm sorry. He was angry for all the right reasons, and nobody ever fed him long enough to find out what else he was.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Rook finds them. Some burn a colour I've never seen, and when I use them, they don't take anything at all.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I stopped asking where they come from. A miracle doesn't owe me an explanation.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Warm fields by spring, if you help me. Full granaries, if the Vale is brave. I can't promise you both by midwinter.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Bring the embers to Ember Keep, and stand beside me when we light it. Not for me. For them.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I remember the Hearth Age. Warm winters. My mother keeping bees on the south wall, singing to them.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: No. That wasn't my mother. That was someone's. I'm sorry, it happens. There are so many of them in here.
lines.direction: a stumble, caught too late; she covers it gently

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: It doesn't matter whose they were. They were real, and I owe every one of them that world back.

options.label: Which of those memories are yours, Maren?
We'll think about it.
No. Not by feeding it lives.
We'll meet you at the Keep, and decide there whose plan it is.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Honestly? Some nights I can't find myself in there. Hundreds of lives, and I have to go looking for mine.
lines.direction: the first time she has said it aloud

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Don't tell my people. They need me to be sure.

options.label: We'll think about it.
No. Not by feeding it lives.
We'll meet you at the Keep, and decide there whose plan it is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She smiles, and is herself again, warm and certain. If it frightened her, nothing in her face admits it.

options.label: We'll think about it.
No. Not by feeding it lives.
We'll meet you at the Keep, and decide there whose plan it is.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: That's all I ask. Think. Then look at the fields this winter, and think again.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: I understand. I'd rather you said no to my face than nodded and lied. The Vale has had enough of that.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: Then I'll see you at the Keep. I hope we're standing on the same side of the flame.

lines.speaker: maren_sorrel
lines.text: The truce holds until sundown. After that, I would rather not be your enemy. But I will be, if I must.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She leaves the water and the white cloth where they are, and walks away along the crater's rim without looking back.
